hook.convey: one whole stretch from start = 0 to finish = 1; stopping exactly halfway → standing on a real spot → 0 and 1 have no name for it → fractions are numbers that live between 0 and 1

use.hi: Cricket ki pitch socho. Ek stump 0 par, doosra 1 par. Batsman run lene bhaaga aur theek beech mein ruk gaya. Woh pitch ki ek pakki jagah par khada hai, toh us jagah ka bhi ek number hai.
use.en: Picture a cricket pitch. One stump at 0, the other at 1. The batsman sets off for a run and stops right in the middle. He's standing on a real spot, so that spot has a number too.

use.hi: Ghar 0 par, school 1 km par. School bus aadhe raaste mein ruk gayi. Na 0 par, na 1 par, beech mein kahin. Us jagah ka bhi number hota hai.
use.en: Home is at 0, school at 1 km. The school bus stops halfway. Not at 0, not at 1, somewhere in between. That place has a number too.

use.hi: Game mein level ka bar 0 se bharna shuru hota hai, aur 1 par level khatam. Abhi bar aadha bhara hai. Matlab woh 0 aur 1 ke beech ke ek number par ruka hai.
use.en: In a game the level bar starts filling at 0, and at 1 the level is done. Right now it's half full. So it has stopped at a number between 0 and 1.

explain.convey: 0 and 1 at the ends; one cut exactly in the middle → 2 equal gaps; the middle mark = 1/2 → 1/2 is a number with its own place, between 0 and 1, not at 2

point.hi: Yeh rahi 0 se 1 tak ki line. Upar theek beech mein ek mark hai, toh upar line ke 2 barabar gaps ban gaye. Is mark ka naam hai 1/2.
point.en: Here's a line from 0 to 1. On top, one mark right in the middle, and now the top of the line has 2 equal gaps. This mark is called 1/2.

pointAlt.hi: Ek roti ko theek beech se kaato toh do barabar tukde milte hain. Line par bhi beech wala mark 0 se 1 ko aise hi do barabar gaps mein baant-ta hai, isliye woh 1/2 hai.
pointAlt.en: Cut a roti right down the middle and you get two equal pieces. The middle mark on the line splits 0 to 1 the same way, into two equal gaps, so it is 1/2.

prompt.hi: {friend} ka kehna hai ki 1/3 toh 3 ke paas aata hai. Tumhe kya lagta hai: 1/3 isi 0 se 1 wali line par hai, ya 3 ke paas?
prompt.en: {friend} says 1/3 goes near 3. What do you think: is 1/3 on this line from 0 to 1, or near 3?

simpler.hi: 1/3 ka neeche wala number 3 dekho: woh batata hai 0 se 1 ko kitne barabar gaps mein kaatna hai. 1/3 unme se ek gap hai.
simpler.en: Look at the bottom number of 1/3, the 3: it says how many equal gaps to cut 0 to 1 into. 1/3 is one of those gaps.

why.hi: neeche ka 3 matlab 0 se 1 ke 3 barabar gaps, aur pehla gap isi line par khatam hota hai
why.en: the bottom 3 means 3 equal gaps from 0 to 1, and the first gap ends right on this line

whyAlt.hi: 1/3 poore 1 se chhota hai, toh woh 0 aur 1 ke beech hi aata hai, 3 ke paas kabhi nahi
whyAlt.en: 1/3 is smaller than one whole, so it comes between 0 and 1, never near 3

simpler.hi: Line ke theek beech mein ek mark hai. Woh line ko do barabar gaps mein baant-ta hai, isliye uska naam 1/2 hai.
simpler.en: There is a mark right in the middle of the line. It splits the line into two equal gaps, so its name is 1/2.

explain.convey: same 0 to 1, now 6 marks inside → 7 equal gaps (gaps = marks inside + 1); bottom number = number of equal gaps in 0 to 1; first mark from 0 = end of 1 gap = 1/7; the name comes from gaps, not marks

point.hi: Wahi 0 se 1 ki line, par ab upar 6 marks hain. Marks mat gino, gaps gino: 7 barabar gaps. Toh 0 ke baad pehla mark hai 1/7.
point.en: Same line from 0 to 1, but now there are 6 marks on top. Don't count the marks, count the gaps: 7 equal gaps. So the first mark after 0 is 1/7.

pointAlt.hi: 0 se chalo: har mark se pehle ek gap aata hai, toh 6 marks ke 6 gaps, aur aakhri mark ke baad 1 tak ek gap aur. Isliye 6 marks ke saath 7 gaps hain, aur 0 ke baad wala pehla mark 1/7 hai.
pointAlt.en: Walk from 0: there is a gap before each mark, so 6 marks give 6 gaps, and one more gap after the last mark up to 1. That's why 6 marks come with 7 gaps, and the first mark after 0 is 1/7.

prompt.hi: Ab line ke neeche dekho. Wahan 0 aur 1 ke beech 7 marks hain, sab barabar doori par. Neeche line kitne barabar gaps mein bati hai?
prompt.en: Now look under the line. There are 7 marks between 0 and 1, all evenly spaced. How many equal gaps does that make below?

why.hi: beech ke marks se gaps hamesha ek zyada, toh 7 marks ke 8 gaps
why.en: there's always one more gap than marks in between, so 7 marks make 8 gaps

whyAlt.hi: neeche chalkar gino: 0 se pehle mark tak ek gap, phir 7 marks mein se har mark ke baad ek gap, toh 1 + 7 = 8 gaps
whyAlt.en: walk along below: one gap from 0 to the first mark, then one gap after each of the 7 marks, so 1 + 7 = 8 gaps

simpler.hi: Upar 6 marks the aur gaps 7, yaani gaps ek zyada. Neeche ke 7 marks par bhi yahi chalega.
simpler.en: On top there were 6 marks and 7 gaps, one more gap. The same works for the 7 marks below.

explain.convey: the same 0 to 1 in 8 equal gaps → more gaps than the 7 before → each gap smaller; 1/8 = first mark, right next to 0; 1/2 still the middle mark (4 of the 8 gaps); more equal gaps in the same whole → each gap shorter → 1/8 sits closer to 0 than 1/7 and 1/2

point.hi: Ab wahi 0 se 1, par upar 8 barabar gaps hain. 7 gaps se zyada gaps, toh har ek chhota gap hai. Pehla mark 1/8, bilkul 0 se chipka hua.
point.en: Now the same 0 to 1, but on top there are 8 equal gaps. More gaps than 7, so each one is a smaller gap. The first mark is 1/8, right up against 0.

pointAlt.hi: Ek chocolate ko 8 barabar tukdon mein todo, toh har tukda 7 tukdon wale se patla hota hai. Line par bhi 8 barabar gaps mein har gap chhota hai, isliye pehla mark, 1/8, 0 ke itna paas hai.
pointAlt.en: Break a chocolate bar into 8 equal pieces and each piece is thinner than with 7 pieces. On the line too, with 8 equal gaps each gap is short, so the first mark, 1/8, sits so close to 0.

prompt.hi: Ab neeche dekho: wahi line 10 barabar gaps mein kati hai. 0 ke zyada paas kaun rukega: 1/8 ya 1/10?
prompt.en: Now look below: the same line cut into 10 equal gaps. Which stops closer to 0: 1/8 or 1/10?

why.hi: 10 gaps wala har gap 8 gaps wale se chhota hai, isliye 1/10 pehle ruk jaata hai, 0 ke paas
why.en: a gap out of 10 is smaller than a gap out of 8, so 1/10 stops sooner, nearer 0

whyAlt.hi: ek hi deewar par do seedhiyaan socho, ek mein 8 barabar paydaan aur ek mein 10: 10 wali seedhi ka pehla paydaan zameen ke zyada paas hota hai, waise hi line par 1/10 pehle rukta hai, 0 ke zyada paas
whyAlt.en: picture two ladders against the same wall, one with 8 equal steps and one with 10: the 10-step ladder's first step is nearer the ground, and in the same way 1/10 stops first on the line, nearer 0

simpler.hi: 8 gaps hue toh pehla mark 1/8 ekdum 0 ke paas aa gaya. Gaps jitne zyada, pehla mark 0 ke utna hi paas.
simpler.en: With 8 gaps, the first mark, 1/8, moved right up to 0. The more gaps, the closer the first mark sits to 0.

problem.hi: Ghar 0 par hai aur school 1 km par. Beech raaste mein 3 bijli ke khambe barabar doori par khade hain. Pehla khamba ghar se kitne kilometre door hai?
problem.en: Home is at 0 and school is at 1 km. Along the road between them stand 3 electric poles, evenly spaced. How many kilometres from home is the first pole?

problemAlt.hi: Socho ek 1 kilometre lambi rassi par 3 gaanthein barabar doori par bandhi hain. Rassi ke shuru se pehli gaanth kitni door hai, wahi nikalna hai.
problemAlt.en: Picture a rope 1 kilometre long with 3 knots tied at equal spacing. How far the first knot is from the start of the rope is what we find.

simpler.hi: Ghar se school tak 1 km ka raasta hai, aur beech mein 3 khambe barabar doori par hain. Pehla khamba kahan hai, yeh dhoondhna hai.
simpler.en: The road from home to school is 1 km, with 3 poles evenly spaced between. We need where the first pole stands.

givens.hi: poora raasta 1 km ka, aur beech mein 3 khambe
givens.en: a 1 km road with 3 poles in between

find.hi: pehle khambe ki doori, kilometre mein
find.en: how far the first pole is, in kilometres

do.hi: Ek line kheencho, ghar 0 par aur school 1 par
do.en: Draw a line with home at 0 and school at 1

why.hi: ghar se school tak ka poora raasta hi humara ek poora hai
why.en: the whole road from home to school is our one whole

simpler.hi: Bas do jagah pakki karo: ghar 0 par, school 1 par. Beech ka saara raasta ek poora hai.
simpler.en: Fix just two spots: home at 0, school at 1. All the road in between is one whole.

do.hi: Khambe mat gino, unke beech ke gaps gino
do.en: Don't count the poles, count the gaps between them

why.hi: beech mein jitne marks hon, gaps hamesha usse ek zyada
why.en: there is always one more gap than marks in between

simpler.hi: Ghar se pehle khambe tak ek gap, phir khambe se khamba, aur aakhri khambe se school tak ek. 3 khambe, 4 gaps.
simpler.en: Home to the first pole is one gap, then pole to pole, then the last pole to school. 3 poles, 4 gaps.

prompt.hi: Raasta 4 barabar gaps mein bata hai, aur pehla khamba ghar se bas ek gap door hai. Woh kitne kilometre par hai?
prompt.en: The road is in 4 equal gaps, and the first pole is just one gap from home. At how many kilometres is it?

reask.hi: 1 kilometre ka raasta 4 barabar gaps mein ho, toh ghar se ek gap door pehla khamba kitne kilometre par hai?
reask.en: If a 1 kilometre road is in 4 equal gaps, how many kilometres from home is the first pole, one gap along?

why.hi: raasta 4 barabar gaps mein bata hai aur pehla khamba theek ek gap par hai
why.en: the road is in 4 equal gaps and the first pole stands exactly one gap along

whyAlt.hi: 4 barabar gaps milkar poora 1 km banate hain, toh ek gap 1 km ka ek chauthai hai, yaani 1/4 kilometre
whyAlt.en: 4 equal gaps make the whole 1 km, so one gap is one quarter of the kilometre, that is 1/4 kilometre

simpler.hi: Poora raasta 1 km ka hai, aur woh 4 barabar gaps mein bata hai. Ek gap 1 km ka kaunsa fraction hai, bas yahi socho.
simpler.en: The whole road is 1 km, cut into 4 equal gaps. Just think what fraction of 1 km one gap is.

answer.hi: pehla khamba ghar se 1/4 kilometre door hai
answer.en: the first pole is 1/4 kilometre from home

why.hi: 4 barabar gaps mein har gap 1/4 kilometre ka hai, aur pehla khamba 0 se theek ek gap par khada hai
why.en: with 4 equal gaps each gap is 1/4 kilometre, and the first pole stands exactly one gap from 0

prompt.hi: Is line par 0 aur 1 ke beech 10 marks hain, barabar doori par. 0 ke baad pehla mark kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: This line has 10 evenly spaced marks between 0 and 1. What fraction is the first mark after 0?

why.hi: 10 marks se line ke 11 barabar gaps bante hain, aur pehla mark ek gap par hai, yaani 1/11
why.en: 10 marks make 11 equal gaps, and the first mark is one gap along, at 1/11

whyAlt.hi: chhota karke dekho: 1 mark ho toh 2 gaps, 2 marks ho toh 3 gaps; isi tarah 10 marks ke 11 gaps, toh pehla mark 1/11
whyAlt.en: try it smaller: 1 mark gives 2 gaps, 2 marks give 3 gaps; the same way 10 marks give 11 gaps, so the first mark is 1/11

simpler.hi: Marks chhodo, gaps gino. 0 se 1 ki line par 10 marks se jitne gaps bane, wahi neeche wala number hai.
simpler.en: Forget the marks, count the gaps. On a line from 0 to 1, however many gaps the 10 marks make, that's the bottom number.

prompt.hi: {friend} ka kehna hai ki 1/11 line par 1/4 ke baad aata hai, kyunki 11, 4 se bada hai. {friend} sahi hai ya galat?
prompt.en: {friend} says 1/11 comes after 1/4 on the line, because 11 is bigger than 4. Is {friend} right or wrong?

reask.hi: {friend} ka kehna hai ki 1/11 line par 1/4 ke baad aata hai: yeh sahi hai ya galat?
reask.en: {friend} says 1/11 comes after 1/4 on the line: is that right or wrong?

why.hi: wahi poora 11 mein bata toh har gap chhota, isliye 1/11 pehle rukta hai, 1/4 se pehle; {friend} galat hai
why.en: the same whole cut into 11 makes each gap smaller, so 1/11 stops sooner, before 1/4; {friend} is wrong

whyAlt.hi: ek pizza 11 logon mein bate toh har ek ko 4 logon wale se chhota tukda milta hai; 1/11 chhota hai, isliye line par 1/4 se pehle aata hai, aur {friend} galat hai
whyAlt.en: share a pizza among 11 and each gets a smaller piece than among 4; 1/11 is smaller, so on the line it comes before 1/4, and {friend} is wrong

simpler.hi: Socho ek roti 4 logon mein bati, ya 11 logon mein. Jis baar tukda chhota mile, woh line par pehle rukta hai.
simpler.en: Imagine one roti shared among 4, or among 11. Whichever way the piece is smaller stops earlier on the line.

prompt.hi: Line 0 se 1 tak 9 barabar gaps mein hai. Kuch log sochte hain ki line par 1/9 ki koi jagah nahi hoti. 1/9 ki jagah 0 ke baad kaunsa mark hai?
prompt.en: The line from 0 to 1 is in 9 equal gaps. Some people think 1/9 has no place on a line. Which mark after 0 is the place of 1/9?

why.hi: 1/9 matlab 9 barabar gaps mein se 1 gap, toh 1/9 ki jagah 0 se ek gap par, pehle mark par hai
why.en: 1/9 means 1 gap out of 9 equal gaps, so 1/9 sits one gap from 0, at the first mark

whyAlt.hi: jaise 7 gaps wali line par 0 ke baad pehla mark 1/7 tha, waise hi 9 gaps wali line par pehla mark 1/9 hai; line par har fraction ki apni jagah hai
whyAlt.en: just as on the line of 7 gaps the first mark after 0 was 1/7, on a line of 9 gaps the first mark is 1/9; every fraction has its own place on the line

simpler.hi: 1/9 ka neeche wala 9 batata hai ki line 9 barabar gaps mein kati hai. Ab socho, 0 se ek gap chalkar kahan pahunchte hain.
simpler.en: The bottom 9 of 1/9 says the line is cut into 9 equal gaps. Now think where one gap from 0 takes you.

den 4 (halves halved, as in e2 and the worked example) → 2nd mark = 2/4 → same spot as 1/2; gap-value thinking, not mark counting

remediation.move: ribbon at a tailor's shop, 0 to 1 m, one line cut in 7 on top and 12 below; marks = chalk marks, gaps = ribbon pieces (said once: each ribbon piece is one gap of the line); marks inside + 1 = pieces; a mark's name comes from counting pieces, not marks; top: 6 marks → 7 pieces → first mark at 1/7 m; then below: first mark at 1/12 m → 12 pieces → 11 marks (the trap says 12)

say.hi: Darzi ka ribbon socho, 0 se 1 metre: upar 6 chalk ke marks, aur ribbon ke 7 barabar tukde. Har tukda line ka ek gap hai. Pehla mark pehle tukde ke end par, yaani 1/7 metre. Naam tukde ginkar milta hai, mark ginkar nahi.
say.en: Picture a tailor's ribbon, 0 to 1 metre: 6 chalk marks on top, the ribbon in 7 equal pieces. Each piece is one gap of the line. The first mark ends the first piece, at 1/7 metre. The name comes from counting pieces, not marks.

simpler.hi: 6 marks, 7 tukde. Tukde gino, toh pehla mark 1/7 metre par hai.
simpler.en: 6 marks, 7 pieces. Count the pieces, and the first mark is at 1/7 metre.

prompt.hi: Ribbon ki neeche wali line par pehla chalk mark 1/12 metre par hai. Neeche kitne chalk ke marks hain?
prompt.en: On the ribbon's lower line the first chalk mark is at 1/12 metre. How many chalk marks are there below?

reask.hi: Pehla chalk mark 1/12 metre par ho, toh ribbon ki neeche wali line par kitne chalk ke marks hain?
reask.en: If the first chalk mark is at 1/12 metre, how many chalk marks are on the ribbon's lower line?

why.hi: 1/12 metre matlab ribbon ke 12 barabar tukde, aur 12 tukdon ke beech 11 marks hote hain
why.en: 1/12 metre means the ribbon is in 12 equal pieces, and 12 pieces have 11 marks between them

whyAlt.hi: 12 tukde banane ke liye ribbon ko kainchi se 11 jagah kaatna padta hai, 12 jagah nahi; har kaat ek mark hai, toh 11 marks
whyAlt.en: to get 12 pieces you cut the ribbon in 11 places, not 12; each cut is a mark, so 11 marks

simpler.hi: Neeche ribbon ke tukde socho: marks tukdon ke beech hote hain, isliye marks hamesha tukdon se ek kam.
simpler.en: Think of the ribbon pieces below: the marks sit between the pieces, so there is always one mark fewer than pieces.

remediation.move: on the then-card's own board (one 0-to-1 line, fifths on top, sixths below, 1/5 marked), naming none of its numbers: both rows are the same whole; a bigger bottom number shares the same whole into more pieces, so each piece is smaller → bigger bottom number = smaller piece; then the child places 1/6: between 0 and 1/5, not after it

say.hi: Upar aur neeche, dono ek hi line hain, 0 se 1 tak: wahi ek poora. Fraction ka neeche wala number jitna bada, wahi poora utne zyada barabar gaps mein bata, aur har gap utna chhota. Bada number matlab bada gap nahi.
say.en: Top and bottom are the same line, 0 to 1: the same one whole. The bigger a fraction's bottom number, the more equal gaps that same whole is cut into, and the smaller each gap. A bigger number does not mean a bigger gap.

simpler.hi: Poora wahi rahe aur gaps zyada hon, toh har gap chhota hota hai. Fraction ka neeche wala number bada ho, toh uska gap chhota hota hai.
simpler.en: One whole, more gaps, so each gap is smaller. When a fraction's bottom number is bigger, its gap is smaller.

prompt.hi: Upar pehla mark 1/5 hai, neeche line 6 barabar gaps mein. 1/6 kahaan aayega: 0 aur 1/5 ke beech, ya 1/5 ke baad?
prompt.en: On top the first mark is 1/5; below, the line is in 6 equal gaps. Where does 1/6 go: between 0 and 1/5, or after 1/5?

why.hi: 6 gaps wala har gap 5 gaps wale se chhota hai, isliye 1/6, 0 aur 1/5 ke beech rukta hai
why.en: a gap out of 6 is smaller than a gap out of 5, so 1/6 stops between 0 and 1/5

whyAlt.hi: 5 gap milkar 0 se 1 bharte hain, aur 6 gap ko bhi wahi 0 se 1 bharna hai, toh 6 waala har gap chhota hoga; isliye 1/6 pehle aata hai, 0 aur 1/5 ke beech
whyAlt.en: 5 gaps fill 0 to 1, and 6 gaps must fill the same 0 to 1, so each of the 6 is shorter; that's why 1/6 comes first, between 0 and 1/5

simpler.hi: 1/6 wala gap 1/5 wale gap se chhota hai. Chhota gap pehle khatam ho jaata hai.
simpler.en: A 1/6 gap is shorter than a 1/5 gap. A shorter gap ends sooner.

say.hi: Ghar se chai ki dukaan tak sadak hai, 0 se 1 km. Upar woh 7 barabar gaps mein bati hai. Khilona chala aur pehle mark par ruk gaya. Woh sadak ki ek pakki jagah par khada hai, aur us jagah ka number hai 1/7 kilometre.
say.en: There's a road from home to the chai stall, 0 to 1 km. On top it's in 7 equal gaps. A toy walks and stops at the first mark. It's standing on a real spot of the road, and that spot's number is 1/7 kilometre.

simpler.hi: Khilona hawa mein nahi, sadak ki ek pakki jagah par khada hai. Us jagah ka bhi number hai, 1/7 kilometre.
simpler.en: The toy isn't floating; it stands on one real spot of the road. That spot has a number too, 1/7 kilometre.

prompt.hi: Neeche wahi sadak 6 barabar gaps mein hai. Khilona neeche 0 ke baad paanchve mark par ruka. Woh kis number par hai?
prompt.en: Below, the same road is in 6 equal gaps. The toy stops at the fifth mark after 0 below. What number is it on?

reask.hi: 6 barabar gaps wali neeche ki sadak par 0 ke baad paanchva mark kis number par hai?
reask.en: On the lower road in 6 equal gaps, what number is the fifth mark after 0?

why.hi: neeche sadak 6 barabar gaps mein hai, aur paanchva mark 0 se paanch gap par hai: ek pakki jagah, 5/6 kilometre
why.en: the lower road is in 6 equal gaps and the fifth mark is five gaps from 0: one real spot, 5/6 kilometre

whyAlt.hi: khilona 6 barabar gaps wali sadak par 0 se 5 gap chala; '6 mein se 5 gap' ko ek number mein bolte hain 5/6 kilometre
whyAlt.en: the toy walked 5 gaps from 0 on a road of 6 equal gaps; '5 gaps out of 6' said as one number is 5/6 kilometre

simpler.hi: Neeche bhi wahi sadak hai, 6 barabar gaps mein. 0 se paanchve mark tak kitne gap hain, gino.
simpler.en: The line below is the same road, in 6 equal gaps. Count the gaps from 0 to the fifth mark.

simpler.hi: Ab upar wala number batayega ki 0 se kitne gap chalne hain.
simpler.en: Now the top number says how many gaps to move from 0.

hook.convey: same 0-to-1 stretch cut into equal stretches; the stop is not the first mark but several stretches on → its name needs two facts: how many equal stretches make the whole (bottom), how many are covered from 0 (top)

use.hi: Cricket pitch ko 4 barabar gaps mein baanto. Batsman 0 wale stump se bhaaga aur 3 gap paar karke ruka. Uski jagah batane ke liye do cheezein chahiye: pitch ke kitne gaps hain, aur usne kitne paar kiye.
use.en: Split a cricket pitch into 4 equal gaps. The batsman runs from the stump at 0 and stops after 3 gaps. To name his spot we need two things: how many gaps the pitch has, and how many he crossed.

use.hi: Game ka loading bar 0 se 1 tak hai, 5 barabar gaps mein. Abhi bar 0 se 2 gap tak bhara hai. Kitna bhara, yeh batane ke liye do number chahiye, neeche wala aur upar wala.
use.en: A game's loading bar runs from 0 to 1, in 5 equal gaps. Right now it's filled 2 gaps from 0. To say how full it is, we need two numbers, a bottom one and a top one.

explain.convey: thirds: bottom 3 → 0 to 1 in 3 equal gaps; top 2 → 2 hops of 1/3 from 0; landing mark = 2/3 → one point, one number, not 2 and 3 separately

point.hi: Is baar upar line 3 barabar gaps mein kati hai, har gap 1/3. 0 se 2 gap chalo, ek, do, aur hum 2/3 par aa gaye. 2/3 ek hi jagah hai, ek hi number.
point.en: This time, on top, the line is cut into 3 equal gaps, each gap 1/3. Move 2 gaps from 0, one, two, and we're at 2/3. 2/3 is one place, one number.

pointAlt.hi: Yahi baat doosre sire se: 2/3 wala mark 0 se 2 gap door hai aur 1 se sirf 1 gap. Upar ke 3 gaps mein se 2 uske peeche hain, isliye uska naam 2/3 hai.
pointAlt.en: The same thing from the other end: the 2/3 mark is 2 gaps from 0 and just 1 gap from 1. Of the 3 gaps on top, 2 are behind it, which is why it's called 2/3.

prompt.hi: Neeche wali line 8 barabar gaps mein kati hai. 0 se 5 gap chalo. Kis fraction par pahunchoge?
prompt.en: The lower line is cut into 8 equal gaps. Move 5 gaps from 0. Which fraction do you land on?

reask.hi: 8 barabar gaps wali neeche ki line par 0 se 5 gap chalkar kis fraction par pahunchoge?
reask.en: On the lower line in 8 equal gaps, which fraction do you reach after moving 5 gaps from 0?

why.hi: har gap 1/8 ka, aur aise 5 gap mile toh 5/8
why.en: each gap is 1/8, and 5 of them make 5/8

whyAlt.hi: 8 barabar tukdon wali chocolate mein se 5 tukde lo toh 8 mein se 5, yaani 5/8; line par bhi 8 mein se 5 gap
whyAlt.en: take 5 pieces of a chocolate bar in 8 equal pieces: 5 out of 8, that is 5/8; on the line it's 5 gaps out of 8

simpler.hi: Fraction ka neeche wala number batata hai ek poore ke kitne barabar gaps, upar wala batata hai 0 se kitne gap chalna hai. 2/3 mein: 3 gaps ki line, aur 0 se 2 gap.
simpler.en: A fraction's bottom number says how many equal gaps one whole has, its top says how many gaps to move from 0. In 2/3: a line of 3 gaps, and 2 gaps from 0.

explain.convey: still thirds: 3 hops of 1/3 → every gap used → land exactly on 1 → 3/3 = 1; top < bottom → stop before 1; top = bottom → reach 1

mustSay.hi: upar wala number aur neeche wala number barabar
mustSay.en: top number and bottom number are equal

point.hi: Upar ki line 3 barabar gaps mein bati hai. 0 se teen gap chalo toh theek 1 aata hai, isliye wahan 3/3 = 1. Jab fraction ka upar wala number aur neeche wala number barabar ho, chalna theek 1 par khatam hota hai.
point.en: The top line is cut into 3 equal gaps. Walk three gaps from 0 and you land exactly on 1, so there 3/3 = 1. When a fraction's top number and bottom number are equal, the walk ends exactly on 1.

pointAlt.hi: Pizza ke 3 barabar tukde hon aur teeno le lo, toh poora pizza aa gaya: 3/3 ek poora hai. Line par bhi 3 mein se 3 gap chalkar hum poore 1 par hote hain.
pointAlt.en: If a pizza has 3 equal pieces and you take all three, you have the whole pizza: 3/3 is one whole. On the line too, 3 gaps out of 3 put us on the whole 1.

prompt.hi: Neeche wali line par har gap 1/5 ka hai. 0 se chalkar theek 1 par pahunchne ke liye kitne gap chalne honge?
prompt.en: On the lower line each gap is 1/5. How many gaps from 0 to land exactly on 1?

reask.hi: Har gap 1/5 ka ho, toh 0 se theek 1 tak kitne gap chalne honge?
reask.en: If each gap is 1/5, how many gaps from 0 to exactly 1?

why.hi: 1/5 ke 5 gap milkar 5/5 banate hain, aur 5/5 = 1
why.en: 5 gaps of 1/5 make 5/5, and 5/5 = 1

whyAlt.hi: ulta socho: 4 gap chalkar tum 1 se theek ek gap pehle ho; 1 par pahunchne ke liye ek gap aur, yaani poore paanch
whyAlt.en: think back from it: 4 gaps leave you exactly one gap short of 1; one more gap reaches 1, so five in all

simpler.hi: 3 barabar gaps wali line par teeno gap chalo toh 1 aata hai. Upar aur neeche ka number ek jaisa, toh chalna 1 par rukta hai.
simpler.en: On a line of 3 equal gaps, move all three and you reach 1. Top and bottom the same, and the walk stops at 1.

explain.convey: each third cut in 2 → 6 equal gaps; the middle = half of the 6 gaps = 3 gaps → 3/6 = 1/2; fewer than half the gaps (2/6) → before the middle; more than half (5/6) → after the middle

point.hi: Ab line ke 6 barabar gaps hain. Theek beech ka mark 3/6 hai, aur 3, 6 ka aadha hai, toh 3/6 = 1/2. 2/6 beech se pehle aata hai, 5/6 beech ke baad.
point.en: Now the line has 6 equal gaps. The mark right in the middle is 3/6, and 3 is half of 6, so 3/6 = 1/2. 2/6 comes before the middle, 5/6 after it.

pointAlt.hi: Roti ke 6 barabar tukde socho: 3 tukde le lo toh theek aadhi roti hai, isliye 3/6 = 1/2 beech mein hai. 2 tukde aadhi se kam hain, toh 2/6 beech se pehle, aur 5 tukde aadhi se zyada, toh 5/6 beech ke baad.
pointAlt.en: Think of a roti in 6 equal pieces: take 3 and you have exactly half, so 3/6 = 1/2 is the middle. 2 pieces are less than half, so 2/6 comes before the middle, and 5 pieces are more than half, so 5/6 after it.

prompt.hi: Isi line par 4/6 kahaan aayega: beech se pehle, ya beech ke baad?
prompt.en: On this same line, where does 4/6 go: before the middle, or after it?

why.hi: beech 3/6 par hai, aur upar ka 4 usse ek zyada, toh ek gap aage, beech ke baad
why.en: the middle is at 3/6, and a top of 4 is one more, so one gap on, after the middle

whyAlt.hi: 6 mein se 4 gap aadhe se zyada hain, kyunki 6 ka aadha 3 hai; aadhe se zyada wala fraction beech ke baad aata hai
whyAlt.en: 4 gaps out of 6 is more than half, since half of 6 is 3; a fraction past half comes after the middle

simpler.hi: Beech 3/6 par hai. Upar ka number 3 se chhota ho toh pehle, bada ho toh baad.
simpler.en: The middle is at 3/6. A top number below 3 comes before it, above 3 comes after.

problem.hi: Ek number line 0 se 1 tak hai. Is par 2/5 ka mark dhoondo.
problem.en: A number line runs from 0 to 1. Find the mark for 2/5.

problemAlt.hi: Socho 1 km ki sadak hai, aur hume woh jagah dhoondni hai jo 2/5 kilometre par hai. Board ki line wahi sadak hai: 0 shuruaat, 1 aakhir.

simpler.hi: 0 se 1 ki ek line hai, aur us par 2/5 dikhana hai. Neeche ka 5 aur upar ka 2, dono kaam aayenge.

do.hi: Ab dekho ek gap kitne ka hai

why.en: 5 equal gaps together make 1 whole

simpler.en: Five gaps make one whole together. So one gap is 1/5 of the whole.

prompt.hi: Ab upar wala number. 0 se utne gap aage chalo. 0 ke baad kaunse mark par ruke?
prompt.en: Now the top number. Move that many gaps on from 0. Which mark after 0 do you stop at?

reask.en: To show 2/5 on this line of 5 gaps, which mark after 0 do you stop at?

why.hi: upar ka 2 kehta hai 1/5 ke do gap chalo, isliye hum doosre mark par rukte hain
why.en: the top 2 says take two gaps of 1/5, so we stop at the second mark

whyAlt.hi: mark ka naam 0 se gine gaps se aata hai, aur ginti 0 ke baad wale mark se shuru hoti hai: 1/5 wala mark pehla, 2/5 wala doosra
whyAlt.en: a mark's name comes from the gaps counted from 0, and the count starts at the mark after 0: the 1/5 mark is the first, the 2/5 mark the second

simpler.hi: 2/5 ka upar wala 2 hai. 0 se ek-ek gap karke chalo, aur gino.
simpler.en: The top of 2/5 is 2. Step from 0 one gap at a time, and count.

why.hi: upar ka 2 kehta hai 0 se 1/5 ke 2 gap chalo
why.en: the top 2 says move 2 gaps of 1/5 from 0

prompt.hi: 0 aur 1 ke beech 5 marks hain, sab barabar doori par. 0 ke baad chautha mark kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: There are 5 evenly spaced marks between 0 and 1. What fraction is the 4th mark after 0?

why.hi: 5 marks se 6 barabar gaps bante hain, aur chautha mark 4 gaps par hai, yaani 4/6

whyAlt.hi: board par seedha gino: 0 se 1 tak 6 gaps hain aur 0 se chauthe mark tak 4 gaps, toh 6 mein se 4, yaani 4/6
whyAlt.en: count straight off the board: 0 to 1 has 6 gaps and 0 to the 4th mark has 4, so 4 out of 6, that is 4/6

simpler.hi: Pehle gaps gino, woh marks se ek zyada hote hain. Phir 0 se chaar gap chalo.
simpler.en: First count the gaps, one more than the marks. Then walk four gaps from 0.

prompt.hi: Do tarah ke gap, 0 se 1 ki line par: 1/4 ke 3 gap, aur 1/8 ke 3 gap. 1 ke zyada paas kaun hai: 3/4 ya 3/8?
prompt.en: Two kinds of gaps on a line from 0 to 1: 3 gaps of 1/4, and 3 gaps of 1/8. Which is closer to 1: 3/4 or 3/8?

why.hi: 1/4 ka gap 1/8 ke gap se do guna lamba hai, toh 3 lambe gap 3/4 tak, 1 ke zyada paas
why.en: a 1/4 gap is twice a 1/8 gap, so 3 long gaps reach 3/4, nearer 1

whyAlt.hi: 1 ki taraf se dekho: 3/4 se 1 tak 1/4 ka ek gap bachta hai, jo 1/8 ke sirf 2 gap hai; 3/8 se 1 tak 1/8 ke 5 gap bachte hain, toh 1 ke zyada paas 3/4 hai
whyAlt.en: look from 1's side: from 3/4 to 1 one gap of 1/4 is left, which is just 2 gaps of 1/8; from 3/8 to 1, 5 gaps of 1/8 are left, so 3/4 is nearer 1

simpler.hi: Gap ginti mein barabar hain, 3 aur 3. Farak gap ki lambai ka hai: 1/4 wala gap lamba hai.
simpler.en: The gap count is the same, 3 and 3. The difference is gap length: a 1/4 gap is longer.

prompt.hi: {friend} ka kehna hai ki 3/4 do number hain, 3 aur 4. 0 se 1 ki line par 3/4 dikhane ke liye kitne mark lagaoge: ek ya do?
prompt.en: {friend} says 3/4 is two numbers, 3 and 4. To show 3/4 on a 0-to-1 line, how many marks do you put: one or two?

why.hi: 3/4 akela ek number hai, toh line par uski sirf ek jagah hai: 0 se 3 gap chalkar, wahi ek mark

whyAlt.hi: jaise ghar ka ek hi pata hota hai, waise hi line par 3/4 ki ek hi jagah hai; 3 aur 4 milkar us ek jagah ka naam batate hain
whyAlt.en: just as a house has one address, 3/4 has one place on the line; the 3 and the 4 together name that one place

simpler.hi: 3/4 ka neeche wala 4 gaps batata hai, upar wala 3 batata hai kitne gap chalo. Chalna jahan rukta hai, wahi 3/4 hai.

simpler.hi: 0 par sirf shuruaat hai. Har gap 1/6 ka. Do gap chalo, toh 2/6.
simpler.en: 0 is just the start. Each gap is 1/6. Move two gaps, and it's 2/6.

prompt.hi: Neeche wali line par 0 aur 1 ke beech 9 marks hain, barabar doori par. 0 ke baad teesra mark kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: The lower line has 9 evenly spaced marks between 0 and 1. What fraction is the third mark after 0?

why.hi: 9 marks se 10 barabar gaps bante hain, aur teesra mark 3 gaps par hai, yaani 3/10
why.en: 9 marks make 10 equal gaps, and the third mark is 3 gaps along, at 3/10

whyAlt.hi: 0 aur 1 ko bhi mark gino toh 11 marks hain, aur unke beech 10 gaps; teesra mark 0 se 3 gap par, yaani 3/10
whyAlt.en: count 0 and 1 as marks too and there are 11 marks with 10 gaps between them; the third mark is 3 gaps from 0, at 3/10

simpler.hi: Pehle gaps gino, marks se ek zyada; wahi fraction ka neeche wala number hai. Fraction ka upar wala number: 0 se teesre mark tak kitne gaps.
simpler.en: First count the gaps, one more than the marks; that is the fraction's bottom number. Its top number: how many gaps from 0 to the third mark.

say.hi: Upar aur neeche, dono taraf 0 se 2 gap chalo, par gap ki lambai alag hai. 1/3 ka gap 1/6 ke gap se do guna lamba hai. Toh 2 chhote gap 2/6 par rukte hain, aur 2 lambe gap 2/3 tak jaate hain.

simpler.hi: Dono taraf do-do gap hain. 1/3 wala gap bada, toh 2/3 aage, aur 1/6 wala chhota, toh 2/6 peeche.
simpler.en: Two gaps each side. The 1/3 gap is bigger, so 2/3 is further on, and the 1/6 gap is smaller, so 2/6 stays back.

prompt.hi: Upar 1/3 ke 2 gap 2/3 tak gaye. Neeche 1/6 ke 3 gap: woh 2/3 se pehle rukenge, ya baad mein?

why.hi: 1/6 ke 3 gap sirf beech tak jaate hain, aur 2/3 beech se aage hai
why.en: 3 gaps of 1/6 reach only the middle, and 2/3 is past the middle

whyAlt.hi: 2/3 tak pahunchne ke liye 1/6 ke 4 gap chahiye, kyunki har 1/3 mein do 1/6 hain; 3 gap ek kam hai, toh pehle ruk jaate hain
whyAlt.en: reaching 2/3 takes 4 gaps of 1/6, since each 1/3 holds two 1/6; 3 gaps is one short, so they stop before

simpler.hi: Do chhote 1/6 gap milkar ek lamba 1/3 gap banate hain. 3 chhote gap, 2 lambe gap se kam padte hain.
simpler.en: Two short 1/6 gaps make one long 1/3 gap. 3 short gaps fall short of 2 long ones.

say.hi: Line par har mark sadak ka ek patthar hai, ek pakki jagah. Khilona jis patthar par rukta hai, wahan uski ek hi jagah hai, toh number bhi ek hi: ek fraction, do alag number nahi.
say.en: Each mark on the line is a stone on the road, one real spot. Whichever stone the toy stops on, it is in one place, so it has one number: one fraction, not two separate numbers.

simpler.hi: Khilona ek hi patthar par khada hai. Ek jagah ka ek hi number hota hai, ek fraction.
simpler.en: The toy stands on one stone. One spot has one number: one fraction.

prompt.en: A stone every 1/8 kilometre; the toy stops at the third stone. {friend} says it's 3 and 8. Say it as one number.

reask.hi: Har 1/8 kilometre par patthar ho, toh 0 ke baad teesra patthar ek number mein kitne kilometre par hai?
reask.en: With a stone every 1/8 kilometre, at how many kilometres is the third stone after 0, as one number?

why.hi: har patthar 1/8 kilometre aage hai, toh teesra patthar 3/8 kilometre par

whyAlt.hi: 3 aur 8 alag-alag bolo toh do jagah ban jaati hain, par khilona ek hi patthar par hai; 8 mein se 3 gap, ek number, 3/8 kilometre
whyAlt.en: say 3 and 8 apart and you get two places, but the toy is on one stone; 3 gaps out of 8, one number, 3/8 kilometre

simpler.hi: Patthar se patthar 1/8 kilometre hai. Shuru se teesre patthar tak aise kitne gap hain, gino.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab line 1 par nahi rukegi: use 2 tak le chalenge, aur dekhenge ki 1 ke aage ke fraction kaise dikhte hain.

hook.convey: one whole is finished and the mover keeps going → the stopping point is past 1 → it needs a fraction name bigger than 1 → the line must go on beyond 1

use.hi: Cricket mein ek run matlab pitch ki poori lambai, yaani 1. Batsman ek run pura karke doosre ke liye bhaaga, aur aadhi pitch par ruk gaya. Woh 1 se aage hai, toh uska fraction bhi 1 se bada hoga.
use.en: In cricket one run is the full length of the pitch, that is 1. The batsman finishes one run, sets off on a second, and stops halfway. He's past 1, so his fraction is bigger than 1.

use.hi: Train station 0 se chali, station 1 paar kiya, aur station 2 se pehle raaste mein ruk gayi. Uski jagah 1 ke aage hai, toh number line ko bhi 1 ke aage le jaana padega.
use.en: A train leaves station 0, passes station 1, and stops before station 2. Its spot is past 1, so the number line has to go past 1 too.

explain.convey: the line does not stop at 1 → it carries on to 2; the second whole is cut the same way → 4 equal gaps per whole, all the same size; 4 gaps from 0 = 4/4 = 1; the gap count from 0 keeps growing past 4

point.hi: Line ab 1 par nahi rukti, 2 tak jaati hai. Upar har poore ke 4 barabar gaps, aur 1 wala mark hai 4/4, yaani 4/4 = 1. 1 ke aage bhi gaps usi size mein chalte rehte hain.
point.en: Now the line doesn't stop at 1; it goes on to 2. On top each whole has 4 equal gaps, and the mark at 1 is 4/4, so 4/4 = 1. Beyond 1 the gaps keep going, same size.

pointAlt.hi: Ek ruler socho: woh 1 cm par khatam nahi hota, 2 cm tak chalta hai. Line bhi waise hi 1 ke aage chalti hai, aur 1 ke baad bhi upar har poore mein 4 barabar gaps hain.
pointAlt.en: Think of a ruler: it doesn't end at 1 cm, it goes on to 2 cm. The line goes past 1 the same way, and after 1 too each whole on top has 4 equal gaps.

prompt.hi: Ab neeche dekho: wahan har gap 1/5 ka hai. 0 se 6 gap chalo. 1 se pehle rukoge, ya 1 ke baad?

reask.hi: Har gap 1/5 ka ho, toh 0 se 6 gap chalkar 1 se pehle rukoge, ya 1 ke baad?

whyAlt.hi: 5 barabar tukdon wale ek pizza se 6 tukde nahi nikalte, doosra pizza kholna padta hai; waise hi 1/5 ke 6 gap ek poore se ek gap aage jaate hain
whyAlt.en: a pizza in 5 equal pieces can't give 6 pieces, you have to open a second one; just so, 6 gaps of 1/5 go one gap past a whole

simpler.hi: Upar har poore mein 4 barabar gaps hain. 4 gap chalkar theek 1 aata hai, aur uske baad gaps rukte nahi, 2 tak chalte rehte hain.

explain.convey: 6 hops of 1/4 from 0: the first 4 hops fill one whole → reach 1; 2 more hops → past 1 → 6/4 = 1 and 2/4; top > bottom → beyond 1

point.hi: Upar dekho, har gap 1/4. 0 se 6 gap chalo: pehle 4 gap 1 tak, phir do gap aur, aur hum 6/4 par, 1 ke aage. 6/4 mein upar ka number bada hai neeche ke 4 se, isliye hum 1 ke aage nikal gaye.
point.en: Look at the top, each gap 1/4. Move 6 gaps from 0: the first 4 reach 1, then two more, and we're at 6/4, past 1. In 6/4 the top number is bigger than the bottom 4, so we went past 1.

pointAlt.hi: Ek jug mein 4 glass paani aata hai: 6 glass daalo toh ek jug bhar jaata hai aur 2 glass doosre jug mein jaate hain. 6/4 bhi aisa hi hai: ek poora, aur uske aage 2/4.
pointAlt.en: A jug holds 4 glasses of water: pour in 6 glasses and one jug fills, and 2 glasses go into a second jug. 6/4 is like that: one whole, and 2/4 past it.

prompt.hi: Is baar neeche har gap 1/2 ka hai. 4/2 is line par kis poore number par aata hai?

why.en: 4/2 is 4 gaps of 1/2, and every 2 gaps make one whole, so 4/2 = 2

whyAlt.en: 2 half rotis make one whole roti; 4 halves make 2 whole rotis, so 4/2 = 2

simpler.hi: 6/4 mein pehle 4 gap se ek poora, yaani 1, aur baaki gap 1 ke aage jaate hain. Upar ka 6 neeche ke 4 se bada, isliye 1 paar ho gaya.
simpler.en: In 6/4 the first 4 gaps make one whole, that is 1, and the rest go past 1. The top 6 is bigger than the bottom 4, so it passes 1.

explain.convey: thirds on a line to 3: every 3 gaps = one whole → 3/3 = 1; group the gaps in threes to find which wholes a fraction has passed; top above 3 → past 1

point.hi: Yeh line 0 se 3 tak hai, har poore ke 3 barabar gaps. Pehle teen gaps 1 par khatam hote hain, wahan 3/3 = 1. Teen-teen gaps ka ek group, aur har group ek poora.
point.en: This line runs from 0 to 3, each whole in 3 equal gaps. The first three gaps end at 1, where it says 3/3 = 1. Take the gaps in groups of three gaps; each group is one whole.

pointAlt.hi: Laddu ginte waqt hum unhe teen-teen ke group mein rakhte hain. Is line ke gaps bhi waise hi gino: har 3 gaps ka group ek poora hai, isliye pehle group ke end par 1 hai.
pointAlt.en: When counting laddoos we put them in groups of three. Count this line's gaps the same way: each group of 3 gaps is one whole, so 1 is at the end of the first group.

prompt.hi: Teen-teen ke group banao: 7/3 mein kitne poore group hain?
prompt.en: Make groups of three: how many full groups are in 7/3?

why.hi: 7/3 ke 7 gaps mein teen-teen ke 2 poore group hain, 6/3 = 2, aur 1 gap bachta hai
why.en: 7/3 has 7 gaps: 2 full groups of three, 6/3 = 2, and 1 gap left over

whyAlt.hi: 7 laddu teen-teen karke rakho: 3, phir 3, aur 1 bacha; 2 poore group, isliye 7/3, 2 ke aage hai
whyAlt.en: set 7 laddoos out in threes: 3, then 3, and 1 left; 2 full groups, so 7/3 is past 2

simpler.hi: Har 3 gaps par ek poora number aata hai: pehle 3 gap par 1, aur aise hi aage.
simpler.en: Every 3 gaps reach a whole number: the first 3 gaps reach 1, and so on.

problem.hi: Ek number line 0 se 2 tak hai. Is par 7/4 ka mark dhoondo.
problem.en: A number line runs from 0 to 2. Find the mark for 7/4.

problemAlt.hi: Ek cycle race 0 se 2 km ki hai, aur ek cycle 7/4 kilometre chalkar ruki. Board ki line par uski jagah dhoondni hai.
problemAlt.en: A cycle race runs from 0 to 2 km, and a cycle stops after 7/4 kilometre. We need its spot on the board's line.

simpler.hi: Is baar line 0 se 2 tak hai, aur us par 7/4 dikhana hai. Neeche ka 4 aur upar ka 7, dono kaam aayenge.
simpler.en: This time the line runs from 0 to 2, and we show 7/4 on it. The bottom 4 and the top 7 both help.

givens.en: 7/4 has 4 on the bottom and 7 on top

do.hi: Line par 0, 1 aur 2 likho, aur har poore ke 4 barabar gaps karo
do.en: Write 0, 1 and 2 on the line, and cut each whole into 4 equal gaps

steps.result: 0 se 2 tak kul 8 bane, har ek 1/4 ka

why.hi: neeche 4 hai, aur 7/4, 1 ke aage bhi ja sakta hai, isliye line 2 tak chahiye
why.en: the bottom is 4, and 7/4 may go past 1, so the line has to reach 2

simpler.hi: 0, 1 aur 2 likho. Har poore mein 4 barabar gaps banao, toh kul 8 gaps honge, aur har gap 1/4 ka hoga.
simpler.en: Write 0, 1, 2. Four equal gaps in each whole, so 8 gaps in all, each one 1/4.

do.hi: Upar ka 7 matlab 7 gap chalna hai, toh pehle 4 gap chalo
do.en: The top 7 means 7 gaps to move, so first move 4

why.hi: ek poore mein 4 gap hote hain, aur 7, 4 se bada hai
why.en: one whole holds 4 gaps, and 7 is bigger than 4

simpler.hi: 7 gap chalne hain. Pehle 4 chalo, tum 1 par aa gaye, kyunki 4/4 = 1.
simpler.en: 7 gaps to move. Move 4 first and you're at 1, because 4/4 = 1.

prompt.hi: Kul 7 gap chalne the, aur 4 gap mein hum 1 tak aa gaye. 1 ke baad aur kitne gap bache?
prompt.en: We had 7 gaps to move, and 4 got us to 1. How many more are left after 1?

reask.hi: 7 gap mein se 4 gap chalkar 1 aa gaya, toh 1 ke baad kitne gap bache?
reask.en: Of 7 gaps, 4 got us to 1; how many gaps are left after 1?

why.hi: 7 mein se 4 gap chal kar hum 1 par pahunche, aur 7 − 4 = 3 gap bache
why.en: 4 of the 7 gaps took us to 1, and 7 − 4 = 3 gaps are left

whyAlt.hi: 1 ke baad ek-ek gap gino aur 7/4 par ruko: ek, do, teen; yaani teen gap aur
whyAlt.en: count gaps one at a time after 1 and stop at 7/4: one, two, three; that is three more gaps

simpler.hi: Kul 7 the, 4 ho gaye. Baaki nikalne ke liye 7 mein se 4 ghatao.
simpler.en: 7 in all, 4 done. Take 4 away from 7 to get the rest.

answer.hi: 7/4, 1 ke baad teesra mark hai, yaani 1 aur 3/4, 2 se bas ek gap pehle
answer.en: 7/4 is the 3rd mark after 1, that is 1 and 3/4, just one gap before 2

why.hi: 7 = 4 + 3: pehle 4 gap se 1 poora hua, baaki 3 gap 1 ke aage gaye
why.en: 7 = 4 + 3: the first 4 gaps make 1 whole, the other 3 go past 1

prompt.hi: Ek line lo, 0 se 2 tak, har poora 3 barabar gaps mein. 5/3 kin do poore numbers ke beech aata hai?
prompt.en: Take a line from 0 to 2, each whole in 3 equal gaps. Between which two whole numbers is 5/3?

why.hi: 3/3 = 1 aur 6/3 = 2, aur 5/3 dono ke beech hai
why.en: 3/3 = 1 and 6/3 = 2, and 5/3 sits between them

whyAlt.hi: 5/3 ke 5 gap mein se pehle 3 gap 1 tak le jaate hain, aur bache 2 gap ek aur poora nahi banate, toh woh 1 aur 2 ke beech rukta hai
whyAlt.en: of 5/3's 5 gaps, the first 3 take you to 1, and the 2 left don't make another whole, so it stops between 1 and 2

simpler.hi: 3 gaps milke ek poora. 5/3 ka upar wala 3 se bada hai, toh 1 ke aage dhoondo.
simpler.en: 3 gaps make one whole. The top of 5/3 is bigger than 3, so look past 1.

prompt.hi: Line 0 se 2 tak. 1/6 ke 11 gap chalo, ya 1/12 ke 11 gap. 0 se zyada door kaun gaya: 11/6 ya 11/12?
prompt.en: A line from 0 to 2. Move 11 gaps of 1/6, or 11 gaps of 1/12. Which goes further from 0: 11/6 or 11/12?

why.hi: 1/6 ka gap 1/12 ke gap se do guna hai, toh 11 lambe gap 11/6 tak, 11/12 se kaafi aage
why.en: a 1/6 gap is twice a 1/12 gap, so 11 long gaps reach 11/6, well past 11/12

whyAlt.hi: 11/12 mein upar ka 11 neeche ke 12 se chhota hai, toh woh 1 se pehle; 11/6 mein upar ka 11 neeche ke 6 se bada hai, toh woh 1 ke aage, isliye 11/6 door hai
whyAlt.en: in 11/12 the top 11 is smaller than the bottom 12, so it's before 1; in 11/6 the top 11 is bigger than the bottom 6, so it's past 1, which makes 11/6 further

simpler.hi: Gap dono taraf 11 hain. Lamba gap kaunsa hai, 1/6 wala ya 1/12 wala, bas yeh socho.
simpler.en: 11 gaps on each side. Just think which gap is longer, the 1/6 one or the 1/12 one.

prompt.hi: Line 0 se 3 tak hai, har poora 5 barabar gaps mein. 2 ke baad doosra mark kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: The line runs from 0 to 3, each whole in 5 equal gaps. What fraction is the 2nd mark after 2?

why.hi: har 5 gaps se ek poora, toh 2 tak 10 gaps hain; 2 gap aur chalo toh kul 12, yaani 12/5
why.en: every 5 gaps make one whole, so 2 is 10 gaps from 0; 2 more gaps make 12, so 12/5

whyAlt.hi: 12 gaps ko paanch-paanch karke gino: 5, phir 5, aur 2 bache; yaani 2 poore aur 2 gap, jo 2 ke baad doosra mark hai, isliye 12/5
whyAlt.en: count 12 gaps in fives: 5, then 5, and 2 left; that is 2 wholes and 2 gaps, the 2nd mark after 2, so 12/5

simpler.hi: Pehle gino 0 se 2 tak kitne gaps hain, phir usme 2 aur jodo. Woh kul ginti upar aati hai.
simpler.en: First count the gaps from 0 to 2, then add 2 more. That total goes on top.

ladder.why: den 4 on 0 to 2, same den and line as e1, e2 and the worked example → 5/4 = one quarter past 1; smallest step beyond 1
den 3, no line given → decide before/after 1 from top vs bottom alone (4 > 3); moves the rule off the picture
den 2 inside a story: 1 km + half km → count in halves → 3/2; build the improper fraction from a real distance

remediation.move: eighth-hops laid end to end on a 0-to-2 line, no squeezing: 8 hops fill 0 to 1 exactly → 1 is full → the 9th hop must go past 1; then below, sixths on laps: 7 hops → 7/6 lap; a fraction is a length, and lengths can exceed one whole

say.hi: Upar har gap 1/8 ka hai, line 0 se 2 tak. Pehle 8 gap 0 se 1 ko poora bhar dete hain, isliye 1 wala mark 8/8 hai. Naunve gap ki jagah andar bachi hi nahi, toh woh 1 ke aage pahunchta hai.
say.en: On top each gap is 1/8, on a line from 0 to 2. The first 8 gaps fill 0 to 1 completely, so the mark at 1 is 8/8. There's no room left inside for the ninth gap, so it lands past 1.

simpler.hi: 8/8 = 1, matlab 0 se 1 bhar gaya. Naunva gap andar nahi aata, 1 ke aage jaata hai.
simpler.en: 8/8 = 1, so 0 to 1 is full. The ninth gap doesn't fit inside; it goes past 1.

prompt.hi: Neeche har lap 6 barabar gaps mein hai. Runner 0 se 7 gap daudta hai. Fraction mein kitne lap hue?
prompt.en: Below, each lap is in 6 equal gaps. A runner runs 7 gaps from 0. How many laps is that, as a fraction?

reask.hi: Har lap 6 barabar gaps ka ho, toh 0 se 7 gap daudkar runner fraction mein kitne lap daudta hai?
reask.en: If each lap is 6 equal gaps, how many laps is 7 gaps from 0, as a fraction?

why.hi: har gap 1/6 lap hai, aur runner ne 7 gap daude, toh 7/6 lap
why.en: each gap is 1/6 of a lap and the runner ran 7 gaps, so 7/6 laps

whyAlt.hi: 6 gap se ek poora lap ho gaya, aur 1 gap aur, toh ek lap aur 1/6; yaani 7/6 lap
whyAlt.en: 6 gaps finish one lap and there's 1 gap more, so one lap and 1/6: 7/6 laps

simpler.hi: Har lap mein 6 gaps, toh neeche 6. Upar woh ginti, jitne gap runner daudta hai.
simpler.en: 6 gaps per lap, so 6 on the bottom. On top, the number of gaps the runner runs.

remediation.move: on the then-card's own board (a 0-to-2 line, fifths on top, tenths below), naming none of its numbers: same top number → same hop count; a bigger bottom number → shorter hops → the same number of hops stops sooner; then the child judges 9/5 against 9/10

say.hi: Jab do fractions ka upar wala number ek jaisa ho, toh dono mein utne hi gap chalne hain; farak gap ki lambai ka hai. Neeche wala number bada ho, toh har gap chhota, aur utne hi gap jaldi khatam ho jaate hain.
say.en: When two fractions have the same top number, both move the same number of gaps; only the gap length differs. A bigger bottom number makes each gap shorter, so the same number of gaps ends sooner.

simpler.hi: Dono mein gap ki ginti ek hai. Bas socho, kiska ek gap lamba hai: upar wali line ka ya neeche wali ka.
simpler.en: The gap count is the same. Just think whose one gap is longer: the top line's or the bottom line's.

prompt.hi: Ek nayi line, 0 se 2, upar har poora 5 barabar gaps mein, neeche 10 mein. 0 se zyada door kaun hai, 9/5 ya 9/10?
prompt.en: A new line, 0 to 2, each whole in 5 equal gaps on top and 10 below. Which is further from 0, 9/5 or 9/10?

why.hi: dono mein 9 gap, par 1/5 wala gap do guna lamba, toh 9/5, 1 ke aage, aur 9/10, 1 se pehle
why.en: both are 9 gaps, but a 1/5 gap is twice a 1/10 gap: 9/5 is past 1, 9/10 before 1

whyAlt.hi: 9/10 toh 1 tak bhi nahi pahunchta, par 9/5 mein pehle 5 gap se hi 1 aa jaata hai aur 4 gap aur bachte hain
whyAlt.en: 9/10 never even reaches 1, but in 9/5 the first 5 gaps already reach 1 and 4 more are left

simpler.hi: Har fraction mein upar aur neeche wala number milao. Upar wala bada ho, toh woh poore ke aage nikal jaata hai.
simpler.en: In each fraction, compare the top and the bottom. If the top is bigger, it goes past a whole.

say.hi: Yeh stations ki line hai, 0 se 2. Har do station ke beech 5 barabar gaps, toh station 1 par 1 = 5/5. Train jahan ruke, woh ek pakki jagah hai, aur us jagah ka ek hi number: 0 se gine hue gap, bata 5.
say.en: This is a line of stations, 0 to 2. Between stations there are 5 equal gaps, so at station 1, 1 = 5/5. Wherever the train stops is one real spot, and that spot has one number: the gaps counted from 0, over 5.

simpler.hi: 5 gap milke ek poora, isliye 1 = 5/5. Train jahan ruke, 0 se wahan tak ke gap gino: woh ginti bata 5, ek hi number.
simpler.en: 5 gaps make one whole, so 1 = 5/5. Wherever the train stops, count the gaps from 0 to there: that count over 5, one number.

prompt.hi: Isi 0 se 2 ki line par ek doosri train station 1 se chali aur 3 gap aage ruki. Woh kis fraction par khadi hai?
prompt.en: On this line from 0 to 2, another train starts at station 1 and stops 3 gaps on. What fraction is it standing on?

reask.hi: Station 1 se 3 gap aage rukne wali train kis fraction par khadi hai?
reask.en: A train that stops 3 gaps past station 1 stands on what fraction?

why.hi: station 1 = 5/5 hai, aur 3 gap aage 5 + 3 = 8, yaani 8/5
why.en: station 1 is 5/5, and 3 gaps on makes 5 + 3 = 8 gaps, that is 8/5

whyAlt.hi: station 2 se ulta gino: 2 = 10/5, aur train usse 2 gap pehle hai, toh 8/5
whyAlt.en: count back from station 2: 2 is 10/5, and the train is 2 gaps before it, so 8/5

simpler.hi: 1 tak pahunchne mein jitne gap lage, usme 3 aur jodo. Yahi jod upar likho.
simpler.en: Take the gaps it takes to reach 1 and add 3 more. Write that sum on top.

prompt.hi: Ek line 0 se 2 tak hai. 0 aur 1 ke beech 6 marks hain, aur 1 aur 2 ke beech bhi 6, sab barabar doori par. 0 se 9 gap chalo toh kis fraction par pahunchoge?
prompt.en: A line runs from 0 to 2. There are 6 evenly spaced marks between 0 and 1, and 6 more between 1 and 2. Which fraction do you reach after moving 9 gaps from 0?

why.hi: 6 marks se har poore ke 7 barabar gaps bante hain, toh har gap 1/7; 0 se 9 gap chalkar 9/7 aata hai, jo 1 ke aage hai.
why.en: 6 marks make 7 equal gaps in each whole, so each gap is 1/7; 9 gaps from 0 reach 9/7, which is past 1.

covered.hi: Aaj ki baat yeh thi ki har fraction ki number line par ek pakki jagah hoti hai: neeche wala number 0 se 1 ke barabar gaps ginta hai, aur upar wala batata hai 0 se kitne gap chalna hai. Jab upar wala number neeche wale se bada ho, toh fraction 1 ke aage aata hai.
covered.en: Today was about every fraction having its own place on the number line: the bottom number counts the equal gaps from 0 to 1, and the top says how many gaps to move from 0. When the top number is bigger than the bottom, the fraction comes after 1.

goodbye.en: That's all for today; see you again.
